output.summary: KEP-2876 proposed adding CEL-based validation expressions (x-kubernetes-validations) to CRD structural schemas so many validation rules can run in kube-apiserver without webhooks. The KEP is marked implemented, stage stable.
output.rationale: Complex CRD validation, especially cross-field rules, previously needed admission webhooks, which complicate CRD development and operations. CEL was chosen because it is lightweight and safe to run in kube-apiserver, and it supports pre-parsing and type checking so syntax and type errors surface at CRD registration. Reviewers also favored self-contained, field-scoped rules that take effect with the CRD manifest, and the design restricts field access to `self` for consistency.

alternatives.option: General-purpose CEL admission for any resource type (raised by liggitt as a possible later mechanism)
alternatives.why_not: The discussion says being self-contained, better scoped, and easier to type-check still has value even if general expression admission were added later, so the CRD-embedded approach was kept and the alternative was to be listed in an alternatives section.
The summary states webhooks significantly complicate the development and operability of CRDs, and the non-goals say webhooks are still needed only for cases such as network calls.

alternatives.option: Allow indexing access to arbitrary property names (e.g. spec["wacky field name"])
alternatives.why_not: jpbetz noted CEL properties are only accessible via field selection, and indexing would lose static type checking; the chosen option 2 limits accessible property names and uses __dot__-style escaping.

alternatives.option: Access the previous object (oldSelf) for transition rules in the first alpha
alternatives.why_not: jpbetz said access to the previous version was punted to a separate PR because many things needed to be figured out, and liggitt was skeptical of ratcheting via this route.

evidence.quote: This KEP proposes that an inline expression language be integrated directly into CRDs such that a much larger portion of validation use cases can be solved without the use of webhooks.
It is sufficiently lightweight and safe to be run directly in the kube-apiserver (since CRD creation is a privileged operation), has a straight-forward and unsurprising grammar
From offline discussions, there seems to be consensus that we should require all fields be accessed via `self`.
No, the KEP still refers to it as `oldObject`. I'd like to take a pass on the support for access to the previous version in a separate PR from this one
We intensively changed to return type instead of the object in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/107090 to address the concern of returning too large object back to the user.
